questions.stemHtml: A phone maker launches this year's model with a slightly longer battery life and a marginally better camera than last year's. This is an example of
questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. Incremental innovation means small, continuous improvements to an existing product, service or process.

B Disruptive innovation creates a new market or enters at the low end with a simpler, cheaper offering. C Radical innovation involves fundamentally new technology. D Business model innovation changes how a firm creates or captures value, not the product's specifications.

questions.stemHtml: According to Clayton Christensen's theory, a disruptive innovation typically

options.textHtml: is a better product launched by a market leader for its most demanding customers
requires the most advanced technology available at the time
starts by serving low-end or new customers with a simpler, cheaper offering and then moves upmarket, eventually displacing established firms
improves an existing product slightly every year

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. Christensen described disruptive innovations as offerings that initially look inferior by mainstream measures but are simpler, cheaper or more convenient; they gain a foothold among overlooked or new customers and improve until they challenge incumbents.

A describes sustaining innovation by incumbents. B is wrong because disruption is about the business approach, not necessarily advanced technology. D describes incremental innovation.

questions.stemHtml: A garment manufacturer redesigns its factory floor so that each shirt passes through fewer hand-offs, cutting production time per shirt by a third. The shirts themselves are unchanged. This is best classified as
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. Process innovation is the introduction of a new or significantly improved method of production or delivery. Here the product is unchanged; only the way it is made has changed.

A fails because the product is the same. C fails because no new market or low-end entry is involved. D would involve changes in pricing, promotion, packaging or placement.

source.title: ProCounsel original (CMAT pattern) - AI-drafted, pending faculty review

questions.stemHtml: A software company stops selling one-time perpetual licences and instead charges customers a monthly subscription for the same software. This change is an example of
questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. A business model describes how a firm creates, delivers and captures value. Changing the revenue model from one-time sales to recurring subscriptions changes how value is captured, even though the software is the same.

A and B fail because the product is unchanged. C fails because the method of producing the software is not what changed.

questions.stemHtml: In the lean startup approach, a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is

options.textHtml: the cheapest possible version of the product, to be sold at the lowest price in the market
the final product launched after all features have been perfected
the version of a new product that lets the team collect the maximum amount of validated learning about customers with the least effort
a product that meets only the minimum legal and safety requirements

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. Eric Ries defines an MVP as the version of a new product that allows a team to collect the maximum amount of validated learning about customers with the least effort. Its purpose is learning, not price or polish.

A confuses 'minimum' with lowest price. B is the opposite of an MVP. D confuses 'viable' with regulatory compliance.

source.title: ProCounsel original (CMAT pattern) - AI-drafted, pending faculty review

questions.stemHtml: In lean startup terminology, a pivot refers to

options.textHtml: a structured course correction that changes one or more fundamental elements of the business to test a new hypothesis, while keeping what has been learned
the decision to shut the business down completely
a sudden increase in marketing spending to boost sales
the sale of the startup to a larger company

questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. Ries describes a pivot as a structured course correction designed to test a new fundamental hypothesis about the product, strategy or engine of growth — for example, changing the customer segment while keeping the technology.

B is closing down, the opposite of pivoting. C is merely a tactical change. D is an exit (acquisition).

source.title: ProCounsel original (CMAT pattern) - AI-drafted, pending faculty review

questions.stemHtml: The feedback loop at the core of the lean startup method is correctly ordered as
questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. In the Build–Measure–Learn loop, a team turns ideas into a product (often an MVP), measures how customers respond, and learns whether to persevere or pivot; the learning then feeds the next round of building.

The other orders do not match the standard loop: you cannot measure customer response before something is built, and learning comes from the measurement.

questions.stemHtml: An entrepreneur funds her new venture entirely from personal savings and the revenue it earns from its first customers, without taking money from outside investors. This is called
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. Bootstrapping means starting and growing a business with the founder's own resources and internally generated revenue, without external equity or loans.

A crowdfunding raises small amounts from many people. C venture debt is borrowing from lenders. D angel investing involves an outside individual investor.

questions.stemHtml: An angel investor is best described as

options.textHtml: a high-net-worth individual who invests personal funds in an early-stage startup, usually in exchange for equity
a bank that gives a startup a collateral-free loan
a fund that invests money pooled from institutions in later-stage companies
a government agency that gives grants to startups

questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. Angel investors are individuals who invest their own money at an early stage (often seed stage), typically for equity or convertible instruments, and frequently also offer mentoring.

B is debt from a bank. C describes a venture capital or private equity fund, which invests other people's pooled money. D is a grant-making body, not an investor taking equity.

questions.stemHtml: Which sequence shows the typical order in which a venture-backed startup raises funds as it grows?

options.textHtml: Series A → Seed → Series B → IPO
Seed → IPO → Series A → Series B
Series B → Series A → Seed → IPO
Seed → Series A → Series B → IPO

questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. Seed funding supports the idea and early product; Series A funds scaling once there is evidence of product-market fit; Series B and later rounds fund expansion; an Initial Public Offering (IPO) lists the company's shares on a stock exchange, typically when it is mature.

Each of the other options places a later stage before an earlier one.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of venture capital (VC) financing?

options.textHtml: The VC firm invests money pooled from limited partners into a portfolio of startups.
The investor takes an equity stake and often a board seat.
The startup must make fixed interest payments to the VC firm regardless of its performance.
The investor expects a few highly successful companies to make up for many failures.

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. Fixed interest payments regardless of performance are a feature of debt. Venture capital is equity: the VC's return comes from the rising value of its stake, realised at an exit such as an acquisition or IPO.

A, B and D are standard features of VC: pooled funds from limited partners managed by general partners, equity with governance rights, and a portfolio approach in which a few large successes compensate for many failures.

questions.stemHtml: A startup wants exclusive rights to use its distinctive logo and brand name on its products. Which form of intellectual property protection is most appropriate?
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. A trademark protects signs — names, logos, symbols — that distinguish one enterprise's goods or services from others'.

A A patent protects inventions. C Copyright protects original literary, artistic, musical and similar works, not brand identity in trade. D A Geographical Indication protects products whose qualities come from a specific region (e.g. Darjeeling tea), not a single firm's brand.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is NOT generally a requirement for an invention to be granted a patent?

options.textHtml: Proven commercial success in the market

questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. The standard patentability criteria are novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness to a person skilled in the field) and industrial applicability. An invention does not need to have been sold, let alone succeeded commercially — in fact, public disclosure before filing can destroy novelty.

A, B and C are the three core requirements.

source.title: ProCounsel original (CMAT pattern) - AI-drafted, pending faculty review

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is protected by copyright?

options.textHtml: The text of an original novel
A new chemical process for making cheaper fertiliser
The idea of a food-delivery app
A brand name used on packaged snacks

questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. Copyright protects the original expression of ideas in literary, artistic, musical and dramatic works (and software code) — the text of a novel is a literary work.

B is an invention, protected by a patent. C fails because copyright protects expression, not ideas. D is protected as a trademark.

questions.stemHtml: A startup making water bottles has fixed costs of ₹2,40,000 per month. Each bottle sells for ₹500 and has a variable cost of ₹300. How many bottles must it sell per month to break even?
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. Break-even quantity = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit, where contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit.

Contribution = ₹500 − ₹300 = ₹200. Break-even = 2,40,000 ÷ 200 = 1,200 bottles. Check: revenue 1,200 × 500 = ₹6,00,000; total cost 2,40,000 + 1,200 × 300 = ₹6,00,000.

A (800) wrongly divides by the variable cost (2,40,000 ÷ 300). C (480) divides by the price (2,40,000 ÷ 500). D (2,000) results from using a contribution of ₹120.

questions.stemHtml: In a SWOT analysis of a small coffee chain, a large international competitor announcing that it will open outlets in the same city would be classified as a
questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. In SWOT, Strengths and Weaknesses are internal to the firm, while Opportunities and Threats are external. A new competitor entering the market is an external factor that could harm the firm — a Threat.

A and B are internal categories. D is external but refers to favourable conditions.

questions.stemHtml: Which statement best describes social entrepreneurship?

options.textHtml: Using entrepreneurial and business methods to address a social problem, with social impact as the primary goal
Running a business that donates a fixed share of its profits to charity while its main aim remains profit maximisation
Any business that is active on social media
Government provision of free public services

questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. A social entrepreneur applies entrepreneurial approaches — innovation, sustainable revenue models, scaling — to a social or environmental problem, and measures success mainly by social impact.

B describes corporate philanthropy: the primary goal is still profit. C confuses 'social' with social media. D is public provision, not entrepreneurship.

questions.stemHtml: In the five-stage design thinking model (Empathise, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), which stage comes immediately after Define?
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. The sequence is Empathise (understand users) → Define (state the problem from the user's point of view) → Ideate (generate many possible solutions) → Prototype (build quick versions) → Test (try them with users). Ideation comes after the problem is defined.

A comes before Define. C and D come later, after ideas have been generated. (In practice the stages can loop back, but the standard order is as above.)

questions.stemHtml: Which section of a business plan gives a concise overview of the entire plan, is placed at the very beginning, and is usually written last?
questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. The executive summary condenses the business idea, market, team, financial highlights and funding needs into a short opening section. Because it summarises everything else, it is normally written after the other sections.

A, B and C are detailed sections dealing with one aspect each.

questions.stemHtml: The Startup India initiative of the Government of India, aimed at building an ecosystem for startups, was launched in
questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. Startup India was launched by the Government of India in January 2016, with an action plan covering simplification of compliance, funding support and incentives, and industry–academia partnerships.

A 2014 is the year Make in India was launched, a separate initiative. B: the initiative was announced in the Independence Day address of August 2015, but its formal launch, with the action plan, took place on 16 January 2016. D does not match.
